node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Angle facts as reasons
node.description: Use named angle facts as reasons when explaining geometric relationships.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Parallel line angle reasoning
node.description: Use corresponding, alternate and co-interior angle facts to justify unknown angles.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Polygon angle reasoning
node.description: Use triangle, quadrilateral and polygon angle sums to justify angle relationships.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Angle chasing explanations
node.description: Write step-by-step explanations for multi-step unknown-angle problems.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Meaning of congruence
node.description: Recognise congruent figures as figures with the same size and shape.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Rigid motion congruence
node.description: Use translations, reflections and rotations to justify that figures are congruent.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Corresponding parts in congruent figures
node.description: Identify matching sides and angles in congruent figures using correspondence.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Triangle congruence criteria
node.description: Use triangle congruence criteria such as SSS, SAS, ASA and RHS to justify congruence.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Congruence problem solving
node.description: Use congruence to solve for unknown sides, angles and geometric relationships.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Meaning of similarity
node.description: Recognise similar figures as figures with the same shape and proportional corresponding side lengths.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Scale factor between figures
node.description: Find and interpret the scale factor between similar figures.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Corresponding sides and angles in similar figures
node.description: Identify corresponding sides and equal corresponding angles in similar figures.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Triangle similarity criteria
node.description: Use AA, SAS and SSS similarity criteria to justify similar triangles.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Similarity missing lengths
node.description: Use similar figures and scale factors to solve for missing side lengths.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Indirect measurement with similarity
node.description: Use similar triangles and scale factors to solve indirect measurement problems.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Definitions theorems and assumptions
node.description: Distinguish definitions, accepted facts, assumptions and conclusions in geometric arguments.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: If then statements in geometry
node.description: Use conditional statements to express geometric relationships and implications.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Two column proof introduction
node.description: Organise statements and reasons in a two-column geometric proof format.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Proofs using congruence
node.description: Use congruence facts and criteria to prove geometric relationships.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Proofs using similarity
node.description: Use similarity facts and criteria to prove geometric relationships and proportional results.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Counterexamples in geometry
node.description: Use counterexamples to disprove overgeneralised geometric claims.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Geometric reasons must be named
node.description: A geometric explanation should name the fact, definition or theorem used to support each step.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Parallel angle reasons justify equality or supplements
node.description: Parallel-line angle facts justify why certain angles are equal or supplementary.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Congruence preserves all lengths and angles
node.description: Congruent figures have equal corresponding side lengths and equal corresponding angles.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Correspondence controls comparison
node.description: Side and angle comparisons depend on matching the correct corresponding parts of figures.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Congruence criteria are sufficient conditions
node.description: Triangle congruence criteria give enough information to conclude that two triangles are congruent.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Similarity preserves angles and scales lengths
node.description: Similar figures have equal corresponding angles and proportional corresponding side lengths.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Scale factor multiplies lengths
node.description: A scale factor multiplies corresponding lengths from one similar figure to another.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Proof links statements and reasons
node.description: A proof connects each statement to a valid reason in a logical sequence.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Counterexample disproves a general claim
node.description: One valid counterexample is enough to disprove a universal geometric claim.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Proof conclusion matches the goal
node.description: The final conclusion of a proof should match the relationship that was required to be shown.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Angle fact without reason
node.description: Learner states an angle value or relationship without naming the geometric fact that justifies it.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Congruence means same shape only
node.description: Learner treats same shape as enough for congruence without requiring same size.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Mismatched corresponding parts
node.description: Learner compares non-corresponding sides or angles when using congruence or similarity.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Scale factor treated as additive
node.description: Learner adds a fixed amount to side lengths instead of multiplying by a scale factor.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Proof as visual observation
node.description: Learner treats what appears true in a diagram as a proof without deductive justification.

edge.rationale: Using named angle facts as reasons is central to geometric angle reasoning.
Parallel-line angle reasoning is a core geometric angle reasoning context.
Polygon angle reasoning applies angle-sum facts to geometric arguments.
Angle-chasing explanations combine multiple angle facts with reasons.
Meaning of congruence is foundational to all congruence reasoning.
Rigid motion is a central way to justify congruence.
Corresponding parts are essential when using congruence.
Triangle congruence criteria are a key congruence reasoning tool.
Congruence problem solving applies congruence facts to unknowns and relationships.
Meaning of similarity is foundational to similarity reasoning.
Scale factor is central to comparing similar figures.
Corresponding sides and angles are essential in similarity reasoning.
Triangle similarity criteria are a key similarity reasoning tool.
Missing-length problems apply scale factor and proportional side reasoning.
Indirect measurement is a common application of similarity.
Proof depends on distinguishing definitions, assumptions and accepted facts.
Conditional statements are common in geometric proof structure.
Two-column proof is a common format for linking statements and reasons.
Congruence proofs are a major family of geometric proofs.
Similarity proofs are a major family of geometric proofs and proportional arguments.
Counterexamples support reasoning about when geometric claims are false.
Using angle facts as reasons requires knowing angle relationships.
edge.failure_signal: Learner uses informal statements rather than named angle facts.

edge.rationale: Parallel-line angle reasoning depends on corresponding, alternate and co-interior angle facts.
edge.failure_signal: Learner misidentifies angle pairs or cannot justify equal and supplementary relationships.

edge.rationale: Polygon angle reasoning builds from triangle and quadrilateral angle sums.
edge.failure_signal: Learner cannot break polygon reasoning into known angle-sum facts.

edge.rationale: Angle-chasing explanations require using angle facts as named reasons across multiple steps.
edge.failure_signal: Learner finds values but cannot justify the reasoning chain.

edge.rationale: Understanding congruence requires recognising shape properties that can match exactly.
edge.failure_signal: Learner treats similar-looking figures as congruent without comparing size and shape.

edge.rationale: Rigid motion congruence depends on transformations that preserve size and shape.
edge.failure_signal: Learner cannot connect translations, reflections or rotations to congruence.

edge.rationale: Corresponding parts reasoning builds from the meaning of congruence.
edge.failure_signal: Learner matches sides or angles by visual position rather than correspondence.

edge.rationale: Triangle congruence criteria depend on identifying corresponding sides and angles.
edge.failure_signal: Learner applies a criterion to mismatched or insufficient information.

edge.rationale: Congruence problem solving often uses triangle congruence criteria and corresponding parts.
edge.failure_signal: Learner proves congruence but cannot use it to solve unknowns.

edge.rationale: Similarity is connected to dilations that preserve shape while changing size.
edge.failure_signal: Learner confuses similar with congruent or visually similar only.

edge.rationale: Scale factor between figures requires understanding the relationship between similar figures.
edge.failure_signal: Learner identifies similar figures but cannot quantify the scale factor.

edge.rationale: Correspondence in similar figures is needed to apply scale factors and equal angles correctly.
edge.failure_signal: Learner uses a correct scale factor on non-corresponding sides.

edge.rationale: Triangle similarity criteria require matching corresponding sides and angles.
edge.failure_signal: Learner applies AA, SAS or SSS similarity to mismatched parts.

edge.rationale: Missing-length similarity problems rely on justified similarity and proportional sides.
edge.failure_signal: Learner sets up proportions with non-corresponding sides or additive changes.

edge.rationale: Indirect measurement applies similar-triangle missing-length reasoning to contexts.
edge.failure_signal: Learner identifies similar triangles but cannot connect the missing length to the context.

edge.rationale: Distinguishing definitions, assumptions and conclusions builds from writing reasoned geometric explanations.
edge.failure_signal: Learner mixes given facts, definitions and conclusions in an argument.

edge.rationale: If-then statements require recognising conditions and conclusions in geometric facts.
edge.failure_signal: Learner cannot distinguish hypothesis from conclusion.

edge.rationale: Two-column proofs require linking statements and reasons in a logical sequence.
edge.failure_signal: Learner writes true statements without valid reasons or sequence.

edge.rationale: Proofs using congruence depend on understanding congruence criteria and corresponding parts.
edge.failure_signal: Learner can solve congruence problems but cannot structure a proof.

edge.rationale: Proofs using similarity depend on similarity criteria and proportional corresponding parts.
edge.failure_signal: Learner asserts similarity without proving the needed criteria.

edge.rationale: Counterexamples require understanding the general claim that is being disproved.
edge.failure_signal: Learner gives an example that supports a claim rather than disproves it.
